objective: The command functions in `stockroom/cli.py` print straight to the process's standard output and error and `main` reads the settings from `os.environ`, so a caller that wants to run a command in-process has to redirect global state. Make the input and output of `main` injectable: give `main` the optional keyword-only parameters `stdout`, `stderr` and `environ`, and thread the streams through the command functions. With none of them given, behaviour is exactly as before. This is a refactor of the plumbing, not of the commands: the text they print, their error messages and their exit codes stay byte for byte the same, and the existing tests keep passing without being edited.
acceptance: `main` has the signature `main(argv=None, *, stdout=None, stderr=None, environ=None)`; the three new parameters are keyword-only and default to `None`

When `stdout` is given, everything a command prints to standard output goes to it; when `stderr` is given, everything a command prints to standard error goes to it (the `warning: N item(s) below reorder level` line and `stockroom: error: <message>`); with both given nothing reaches the real streams, and when both are the same object the lines appear in the order they were printed

An omitted stream stands for the process's `sys.stdout` or `sys.stderr` as they are when `main` runs, not as they were when the module was imported, so output redirected or captured around the call is honoured

When `environ` is given, the `STOCKROOM_*` settings are read from that mapping (any `Mapping`) and the process environment is ignored; when it is omitted the process environment at the time of the call is used
The output of argparse itself (`--help`, `--version`, usage errors and their `SystemExit` codes) is unchanged and still goes to the real streams whatever is injected

For `items`, `stock`, `sales` and `price`, including their data errors, settings from the environment and from `--config`, the exit code, stdout and stderr are identical to what they were before the change, both with injected streams and without
In `stockroom/cli.py` every `print` call names its target stream with `file=`, and each of `sys.stdout`, `sys.stderr` and `os.environ` is referred to at most once
